What We Developed:
Interstellar Continuum is an educational 2D space exploration and mission-management simulation built with TypeScript and PixiJS. Players assume the role of Mission Director of an independent Earth-based agency, progressing from suborbital sounding probes to interplanetary expeditions. The game integrates an interactive headquarters campus, modular rocket staging and physics validation, launch operations, Solar System orbital mapping across 28 celestial bodies, satellite communications, and surface rover science.

How It Addresses the Challenge:
The simulation demystifies complex aerospace engineering and orbital mechanics through intuitive, accessible mechanics. By coupling deep systems (propulsion budgets, Delta-V staging, payload limits, and contract funding) with streamlined 1-click workflows, directional waypoints, fast-travel shortcuts, and responsive keyboard/touch controls, players of all backgrounds can design, test, and launch missions without friction.

Why It Is Important:
Space systems engineering and interplanetary science often feel intimidating. Interstellar Continuum transforms authentic STEM concepts—Tsiolkovsky rocket equations, telemetry downlinks, and planetary science—into an engaging, visually polished experience. It inspires curiosity about space exploration and empowers players to understand the real engineering decisions behind humanity’s future among the stars.

Project Overview: INTERSTELLAR CONTINUUM

1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

INTERSTELLAR CONTINUUM is an educational 2D space exploration, rocket engineering, and mission-management simulation. The player commands an independent space agency on Earth and guides its expansion across the Solar System through strategic decision-making, authentic aerospace engineering, and scientific exploration.

Core Gameplay Loops & Systems:

  • Headquarters Campus Exploration: Walk or fast-travel across a living aerospace campus featuring 12 operational facilities, including the Mission Operations Centre (MOC), Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB), Spacecraft Cleanrooms, Launch Complex Pad Alpha, and R&D Laboratories.
  • Modular Rocket Engineering & Physics Validation: Design multi-stage launch vehicles using real engineering parameters—dry vs. wet mass, thrust-to-weight ratios (TWR), specific impulse (IspI_{sp}Isp​), aerodynamic fairings, and Delta-V budgets modeled with Tsiolkovsky rocket equation principles. A 7-category validation engine checks staging, structural integrity, and mission readiness before rollout.
  • Flight Readiness & Launch Operations: Manage pad rollout, cryogenic propellant loading, range safety, umbilical tower disconnects, and cinematic countdown sequences. A streamlined 1-click Auto-Prepare Flight pipeline eliminates repetitive logistics for younger or casual players while preserving underlying physical fidelity.
  • Orbital Simulation & Solar System Map: An interactive orbital map spanning 28 celestial bodies (Sun, planets, dwarf planets, major moons) displaying real Keplerian semi-major axes, gravity, atmospheric compositions, radiation metrics, and transfer windows.
  • Payload & Scientific Exploration: Equip scientific sensors, spectrometers, atmospheric probes, and robotic rovers with energy storage, sample drills, and autonomous hazard-avoidance navigation.
  • Deep Space Communications & Agency Economy: Balance grants, commercial contracts, sponsor agreements, and research datasets while deploying satellite constellations to maintain line-of-sight signal coverage.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Intuitive STEM Education: Replaces dry aerospace textbooks with tactile, hands-on experimentation. Players intuitively learn why multi-staging is required, how gravity wells dictate fuel requirements, and how orbital transfer windows work.
  • Dual-Layer Gameplay Accessibility: Accommodates diverse audiences—young learners and casual players can use 1-click quick-build and auto-prepare workflows to experience immediate rocket launches, while simulation enthusiasts can fine-tune engine thrust curves and payload mass fractions.
  • Zero-Friction Web Delivery: Runs entirely in modern web browsers without installations, heavy downloads, or native plugins.

3. What Is the Intended Impact?

  • Inspiring Future Aerospace Enthusiasts: Spark interest in astronomy, physics, and computer science among students and aspiring engineers.
  • Educational Empowerment: Serve as an interactive learning laboratory for classrooms, coding clubs, and science competitions.
  • Demystifying Space Science: Demonstrate that space exploration is a multifaceted team endeavor requiring financial sustainability, logistics, communications, and testing—not just building rockets.

4. Tools, Coding Languages & Technology Stack

  • Languages: TypeScript 5.x (Strict Mode, 100% type safety, zero any shortcuts in production code).
  • Rendering Engine: PixiJS 8.x (WebGL2 hardware-accelerated 2D pipeline with procedural geometry, custom shaders, and crisp pixel-art styling).
  • Build & Development: Vite 5.x (ultra-fast Hot Module Replacement and ES module bundling).
  • Quality Assurance & Testing: Vitest (comprehensive test harness containing 158 test suites and 1,002 automated unit/integration tests verifying collision math, orbital physics, UI state machines, and contract lifecycles).
  • Fonts & Visual Assets: Custom procedural retro pixel typography (Silkscreen, VT323, Press Start 2P), procedural vector graphics, and CSS3 crisp-edge rendering.
  • Version Control & Coordination: Git branch-based feature isolation and integration verification (integration/final-release-candidate).

5. How Is the Project Creative?

  • Seamless Fusion of Micro & Macro Gameplay: Blends ground-level top-down RPG character movement across a facility campus with high-level aerospace engineering CAD builders and macro-scale Solar System orbital navigation.
  • Aesthetic Cyber-Retro Aerospace Art Direction: Features an intentional 2D orthographic pixel-art aesthetic inspired by classic NASA telemetry monitors, mission control screens, and vintage space adventure games.
  • Procedural Sound and Visual Effects: Visual rocket exhausts, flame trenches, dithered turf rendering, stepped facility shadows, and retro telemetry styling bring aerospace facilities to life procedurally without bloated media asset files.

6. What Factors Did the Team Consider?

  • Cognitive Load vs. Scientific Authenticity: Rocket equations and orbital mechanics can be daunting. We carefully designed the UI with progressive disclosure—surfacing simple "Flight Ready" badges upfront while keeping deep numerical readouts (Delta-V, TWR, specific impulse) accessible for exploration.
  • Responsive Controls & UX: Every interaction supports dual input paths: mouse click/tap and intuitive keyboard shortcuts (Space, Enter, E, WASD, Esc).
  • Performance & Frame Rate Stability: Maintained a 60 FPS budget across all scenes via frustum culling, container pooling, layered depth sorting, and disabling expensive sub-pixel anti-aliasing in favor of sharp pixel rendering.
  • Extensibility & Modularity: Architected with decoupled event buses, registries, and service locators, making it effortless to add new celestial destinations, rocket engines, or mission contracts in the future.
